
spec2def(syssetup.dll syssetup.spec)

# syssetup.dll — Rust cohabitation flip (FULL: all 8 compiled *.c → syssetup-rust).
#
# The system setup DLL: the second-stage GUI wizard (welcome/product/owner/computer/locale/
# date-time/theme/process/finish pages), the account and security-policy writer that talks to
# LSA and SAM, the network-component installer, the setup action log, and the PS/2 mouse
# property page. syssetup_stubs.c stays C: it is GENERATED by spec2def, a build product.
#
# rust_varargs_shim.c is NOT a translation reverted to C. syssetup has two C-variadics and
# stable Rust can DECLARE but not DEFINE one (`va_start` is only legal inside a c_variadic fn,
# rust-lang/rust#44930), so each entry point lives there, does the va_start, and tail-calls the
# fixed-arity `*_v` twin in syssetup-rust that holds the whole translated body.
# pSetupDebugPrint is `@ varargs` in syssetup.spec, so that file owns a real DLL export.
#
# Profile decisions (gen_driver_types.sh), all load-bearing:
#   * BLOCKLIST_FUNCS_FROM_CRATE — syssetup is a thin driver of other people's APIs
#     (setupapi/samlib/advapi32/userenv/comctl32/shell32), so hand-writing the surface would be
#     several hundred prototypes, each of which links and then corrupts silently if it is wrong
#     by one pointer level.
#   * MACRO_SIGNED=0, and that was MEASURED, not reasoned. syssetup looks exactly like aclui and
#     netcfgx — wizard.c alone is 3.4K lines of property-sheet page procs — and the resemblance
#     argument said 1. Whole-crate check said 483 errors SIGNED against 432 UNSIGNED, because it
#     spends more time handing constants to unsigned Win32 parameters than comparing them.
#   * UNBLOCK of DLGPROC and the PROPSHEET containers — Rust compares fn-pointer ABIs NOMINALLY,
#     and ntdll-sys spells each callback with the arch's literal convention. This island owning
#     them is what lets ONE `extern "system"` page proc serve all three targets.
#   * REAL_UNIONS=1 — PROPSHEETPAGE/PROPSHEETHEADER are half anonymous union, and the C
#     flattens them (`psp.pszTemplate = ..`), which the `__BindgenUnionField<T>` emulation
#     cannot accept.
set(SYSSETUP_RUST_WORKSPACE_DIR "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/lib/rust")
if(ARCH STREQUAL "i386")
    set(SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET "i686-pc-windows-gnu")
elseif(ARCH STREQUAL "amd64")
    set(SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET "x86_64-pc-windows-gnu")
elseif(ARCH STREQUAL "arm64")
    set(SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET "aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm")
endif()
rust_storage_target(SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/rust-syssetup-target" syssetup-rust)
set(SYSSETUP_RUST_LIB "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/libsyssetup_rust.a")
rust_crate_sources(SYSSETUP_RUST_SRCS "${SYSSETUP_RUST_WORKSPACE_DIR}" syssetup-rust)
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT ${SYSSETUP_RUST_LIB}
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
        CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET_DIR}
        cargo build --release --target ${SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET}
            -p syssetup-rust
            --manifest-path ${SYSSETUP_RUST_WORKSPACE_DIR}/Cargo.toml
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
        ${SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET_DIR}/${SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET}/release/libsyssetup_rust.a
        ${SYSSETUP_RUST_LIB}
    DEPENDS ${SYSSETUP_RUST_SRCS}
            ${SYSSETUP_RUST_WORKSPACE_DIR}/syssetup-rust/Cargo.toml
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${SYSSETUP_RUST_WORKSPACE_DIR}
    COMMENT "Building syssetup-rust (${SYSSETUP_RUST_TARGET})"
)
add_custom_target(rust_syssetup DEPENDS ${SYSSETUP_RUST_LIB})

# All 8 compiled *.c → syssetup-rust (src/syssetup/*.rs), kept on disk per the never-delete rule.
#   classinst.c dllmain.c install.c logfile.c netinstall.c proppage.c security.c wizard.c
# list(APPEND SOURCE
#     classinst.c
#     dllmain.c
#     install.c
#     logfile.c
#     netinstall.c
#     proppage.c
#     security.c
#     wizard.c
#     precomp.h)

list(APPEND SOURCE
    rust_varargs_shim.c
    # addons.c — NEW upstream TU since the fork (setup-time addon installation). Not built:
    # its only caller, install.c, is Rust here (syssetup-rust), so the C would link as dead
    # weight. Port it to syssetup-rust to pick the feature up.
    #addons.c
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/syssetup_stubs.c)

add_library(syssetup MODULE
    ${SOURCE}
    syssetup.rc
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/syssetup.def)

set_module_type(syssetup win32dll UNICODE)
# libsyssetup_rust.a FIRST so its #[no_mangle] symbols win.
target_link_libraries(syssetup ${SYSSETUP_RUST_LIB} uuid wine tzlib ${PSEH_LIB})
# lld first-match: compiler_builtins in the Rust staticlib and libgcc both carry the 64-bit
# division helpers (__udivdi3/__divdi3). Same code, two copies — take the first.
target_link_options(syssetup PRIVATE LINKER:--allow-multiple-definition)
add_dependencies(syssetup rust_syssetup)
add_importlibs(syssetup advapi32 gdi32 user32 samlib userenv comctl32 setupapi rpcrt4 ole32 shell32 shlwapi msvcrt kernel32 ntdll)
add_cd_file(TARGET syssetup DESTINATION reactos/system32 FOR all)
